suggestion: Split test 1 into three: (1) default resolves to blocking with no configuration; (2) tp set --workflow audit_converge_on=bogus and tp set --project ... exit 2 with the hint naming blocking and all; (3) a stored bogus value winning resolution makes each consuming audit command exit 1 with the same hint. Name the two layers that actually exist for this field in §2 rather than pointing at the five-layer chain.

finding: Test 4 pins two literal round numbers against mutable repository state and does not say how it reads it. spec/.tp-review/0.35.0/ is live loop state: recording a tenth audit round there, or editing any of the nine ndjson files, flips the expected values, and a snapshot-audit-round-10.md already exists in that directory from a round that was emitted but never recorded -- so a tenth entry is not hypothetical. Test 4 also must not invoke tp against the live spec: scripts/check-suite-state.sh wraps the suite in a before/after hash of spec/.tp-review/ precisely because a test that runs tp on a spec still sitting in the repository advances rounds it does not own (v0.36.0 §6.1 S1). §7 says the replay 'reads status and severity off recorded rows and needs no spec snapshot', which is the right property, but it stops short of saying the test is read-only and never calls tp against spec/0.35.0.md.
suggestion: Say in test 4 that the replay is a pure function over copies of the recorded rows -- read-only, no tp invocation against the live spec, or a relocatedSpec-style copy into t.TempDir() -- and derive the expected round numbers from a stated rule rather than pinning 3 and 9 as literals, so the test fails loudly with a wrong verdict rather than silently with a longer history. I verified the current numbers hold: for 0.35.0, rounds 2 and 3 carry zero error rows and rounds 8 and 9 are 200/200 PASS.

finding: Test 4 pins two literals (blocking converges at round 3, all at round 9) against the live spec/.tp-review/0.35.0/ round files in the working tree. Those files are writable state, and this very release makes them semantically live: §3 lets tp audit --resolve write a wontfix/duplicate disposition into a recorded row and have it change a finding count. So dispositioning any old v0.35.0 row -- or any future repair that rewrites those rounds -- silently moves a gate expectation. CLAUDE.md already treats spec/.tp-review/ as state the suite must not disturb (check-suite-state.sh hashes it before and after).
suggestion: Copy the nine round files into a frozen testdata fixture and replay against that, or derive the expectation from the fixture rather than asserting 3 and 9 as literals. Keep the recorded-history claim in the spec as prose; do not make a mutable corpus a gate input.

finding: 'engine/reviewconvergeon.go is twenty-four lines'. Verified correct today — the file is exactly 24 lines, two constants, a hint string and ValidReviewConvergeOn. Raising it anyway because it is a measured constant in prose with nothing binding it, the class CLAUDE.md records as going stale faster than a release, and because the number does no work: the argument is that the twin is small and shared, which the following clause already says. Recommendation, stated plainly rather than left as an observation: LEAVE the sentence, DROP the number. Rewrite to 'engine/reviewconvergeon.go is two constants, a hint string, and a predicate shared by the setter and every consumer.' That keeps the whole force of the point and removes the only part of it that can become false. Do not replace the number with a command that re-derives it — CLAUDE.md records that an under-specified recipe is worse than a stale number, because it can appear to confirm the opposite of what it defends.
suggestion: Delete 'is twenty-four lines:' and keep the enumeration that follows it.

finding: 'v0.36.0's rounds 12 and 13 produced two error-severity findings.' Counted from the recorded rounds: audit-round-12.ndjson carries 2 non-PASS rows, both severity error; audit-round-13.ndjson carries 3, of which 2 are error. That is four error rows across the two rounds, not two. The claim may be counting distinct defects rather than rows, which would be the more useful number, but the sentence does not say which and the two readings differ by a factor of two in a sentence the section calls 'one caveat this release must carry'. CLAUDE.md names this class directly — never assert a quantifier you did not count; bind the claim to an artifact or let a guard enforce it.
suggestion: State both numbers and their basis: 'four error-severity rows, two distinct defects (guards certifying a CI step that never runs), across audit-round-12.ndjson and audit-round-13.ndjson'. The row count is derivable from the files, so it cannot rot; the defect count is a judgement and should be labelled as one.

finding: §6 Non-Goal 4 fences off review convergence, which also fences off the one question an economist would ask before adding the knob: whether one converge_on could govern both phases instead of two. The second knob is not one field — in this codebase a settable workflow field costs a case in engine/projectconfig.go, model/projectconfig.go, model/workflow.go, cli/config.go, cli/config_extract.go, cli/set.go, cli/set_project.go and cli/validate_project.go, plus a row in REFERENCE.md and SKILL.md and resolution through five layers. The answer is probably that two knobs are right, since the phases can legitimately differ and a rename would be breaking; the spec should say so in a line rather than let the Non-Goal foreclose it silently.
suggestion: Add one sentence to §2 saying why the policy is per-phase rather than shared, so the second knob is a decision rather than an inherited shape.

finding: Tests 7 and 8 are the two entries in §7 that cannot fail for the reason they are there. Test 8 ('a cycle whose spec never changes records an identical streak to today's') passes unchanged if §4 is never implemented at all, so it is only informative beside a test 6 that can fail -- and test 6 currently cannot, because no key is named (see the §4 row). Test 7 ('the reset does not delete or rewrite any recorded round') needs scoping: tp audit --record necessarily appends an entry to state.json and writes a new round file, so 'does not rewrite' has to mean the entries recorded BEFORE this invocation, compared field-by-field.
suggestion: Keep both, and make them falsifiable: test 8 as a differential -- the same fixture recorded twice, once with an unchanged spec and once with a changed one, asserting the streak differs between the two runs; test 7 as a byte comparison of the prior audit_rounds entries (round, file, findings, clean, spec_hash, roles_hash, recorded_at) before and after the reset-triggering record. On the recommendation the brief asks for: leave test 8 in -- it is the only clause defending against an over-eager reset -- but it earns its place only in the differential form.
